(These links work once Part II is set up.)

journals.name: 16 — STRAHD MOCKERY DECK
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/01 — Finale Journals

pages.name: Targeted lines
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

General

  • “There you are. I was beginning to think you had mistaken surviving for arriving.”
  • “An Unkindness of ravens. You circle death so faithfully.”
  • “You have killed me before. Usually you don't remember.”
  • “The book told you? How terribly rude.”

Damien

  • “How many voices have you collected, Damien? I wonder which one answers when nobody else is listening.”
  • “You drank monstrosity rather than die. Do stop pretending we have nothing in common.”

Vesper

  • “Hold your little sun higher, Vesper. Ravenloft has swallowed dawn before.”

Bunch

  • “You are the one I find genuinely perplexing. Everyone else brings scars. You keep bringing hope.”

Legna

  • “Your Queen keeps returning you. Mine never learned to let go either.”
  • “Finn is here, you know. You did say you wanted to save him.”

Thorgrinn

  • “Your brother mourned you.”
  • “What will he call you when he sees you again? Brother? Machine? Miracle?”
  • “Your brother left you a box. He expected you to understand the lock.”

Use these as ingredients, not a script. The macro can pick from them when you need a line quickly.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 17 — ENCOUNTER TUNING
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/01 — Finale Journals

pages.name: Powerful-party controls
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Do not solve difficulty by doubling HP

If the Unkindness is deleting encounters too quickly, increase battlefield pressure:

  • Bring a mist-escaped bride back in Phase II at about 40 HP.
  • Use Strahd's movement more aggressively.
  • Activate another environmental problem.
  • Separate the artifact-light carrier from the rest of the party.
  • Make the Heart Chains matter tactically.
  • Collapse safe ground rather than adding AC.

If the party arrives depleted:

  • Reduce bride HP by 15–20%.
  • Increase the Abbot's miracle.
  • Let Strahd genuinely grant the short rest.
  • Delay one Castle Action.

The Sunsword, Holy Symbol and Tome should make the finale possible. Never respond to the players earning them by making Strahd immune to them.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: The final name rule
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Who owns “the Unkindness”?

During the brides Strahd says the Unkindness.

During Phase I he may even say my Unkindness.

During Phase II he begins using names.

During Phase III he never calls them the Unkindness again.

After Strahd's permanent death, let Damien, Vesper, Bunch, Legna or Thorgrinn be the first person to use the name again.

This time it belongs to them.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 03A — THE WAR OF BROKEN GODS
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/01 — Finale Sequence

pages.name: Arrival — The Prisoners Return
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽
Azrathox banks toward Ravenloft as lightning exposes every tower at once. Then the graveyard below the castle rises.

Not the dead. The earth itself.

Two immense horns push through the soil as a shape of bone, shadow and green corpse-light hauls itself toward the walls. At the same instant, every window in Ravenloft begins to bleed upward. The blood does not fall. It climbs, gathering above the castle into a red-black eclipse.

The infernal seal binding your contracted pit fiend burns hot enough to smoke.

From the battlements Strahd looks first at Orcus. Then at the living wound in the sky.

For perhaps the first time, he does not smile.

“You broke their cages,” he says. “Very well, Unkindness. Let us discover which of us they came to collect.”

Intent

Orcus: kill Strahd permanently, seize the accumulated soul/death-energy of the Domain, and punish anyone who denies him the harvest.

Vampyr: reclaim the covenant, rebind or replace Strahd, and punish the “metal dwarf” who shattered its prison.

Strahd: make the Unkindness solve his Dark Power problem, then kill them once the field is cleaner.

The Unkindness: whatever the players decide. They may help any side temporarily without becoming that side’s servants.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Three Fronts, Not Four Initiative Blocks
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Pressure & Claim

TrackStartAt 4At 6
Orcus Pressure2Graves rupture; Orcus gains an extra Intervention this scene.Orcus breaches Ravenloft fully; his manifestation gains +40 temporary HP and immediately Soul Hooks one resurrected PC.
Vampyr Claim2Black Sun thickens; vampires gain 10 temporary HP at the start of their next scene.Vampyr establishes three Covenant Hooks and can attempt to rebind Strahd the first time he reaches 0 HP.

At the end of each major combat round/scene, an unattended Dark Power advances by 1. A deployed ally prevents the advance on its assigned front. Direct party success may reduce the track by 1 or 2.

Do not advance both tracks merely because time passed during roleplay. Advance them when a tactical opportunity was actually left uncontested.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Helping the Enemy Is Allowed
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Temporary cooperation

Help Orcus: he can suppress Strahd’s regeneration for a round or tear open a route through Ravenloft. Every deliberate cooperation adds +1 Orcus Attention. Orcus does not become friendly.

Help Vampyr: it can suppress Strahd’s Black Sun veil, reveal a blood-route through the castle, or yank Strahd out of wall-phasing. Every cooperation adds +1 Vampyr Attention and may create a Covenant Hook.

Help Strahd: he may cancel one castle hazard, reveal an anchor, or spend a legendary action attacking a Dark Power instead of a PC. This is not redemption. It is a prisoner fighting his jailers.

Help neither: hardest route, but it limits future claims. Reward intelligent neutrality rather than punishing it.

Target priorities

Orcus prefers Strahd → pit fiend → Vampyr → death-defying PCs. Vampyr prefers Strahd/Tatyana/Finn → Thorgrinn/Damien → Sunsword bearer → Orcus. Strahd changes targets whenever doing so makes the Unkindness solve a problem for him.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 03B — DEPLOY THE MONSTERS YOU BEFRIENDED
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/01 — Finale Sequence

pages.name: Azrathox, Scourge of the Silver Wing
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Azrathox

The Unkindness recruited an ancient red dragon rather than killing him. That decision must matter here.

DeploymentEffect
Against OrcusPrevents Orcus Pressure increasing. Once per scene dragonfire can erase a mass-undead complication without a combat.
Against VampyrPrevents Vampyr Claim increasing. Once per scene cauterize a Blood Heart: it loses 15 HP and cannot reform that round.
Against RavenloftStrahd cannot close the roof/bridge route with gargoyles and bats; cancel one castle-wide Lair Action per scene.

Empathy payoff: if Bunch reminds Azrathox what she taught him about love, once during the finale he may protect a creature rather than treasure: take the consequence of one failed front on himself and gain 1 Strain.

At 3 Strain he withdraws injured rather than dies automatically.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: The Contracted Pit Fiend
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Infernal Ally

The contract is the canon anchor: the pit fiend is freed from its containment, causes chaos at Ravenloft, helps defeat Strahd, and does not harm the adventurers. Its true name is deliberately not invented here.

Its default response to Orcus is immediate hostility. A devil may hate Strahd, but a Demon Prince walking into the same battlefield is a much older problem.

Demonbreaker deployment

While assigned to Orcus, prevent +1 Orcus Pressure at each front tick. After three successful containment beats, unlock Hellchain: Orcus cannot use a reaction or Legendary Resistance until the end of the next round.

The Healer trigger

Orcus eventually impales or crushes the pit fiend’s infernal heart. The fiend will die at the end of the next round unless Damien spends his action preserving it. At that same moment Strahd or Orcus should be visibly vulnerable. This is Madam Eva’s choice between the hand that strikes and the hand that saves.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 03C — ORCUS: THE HARVEST OF DENIED DEATH
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/02 — Dark Powers

pages.name: What Orcus Wants
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Orcus does not want Strahd’s throne

He wants the ending Strahd has denied for centuries: the death of the Darklord, the released dead, and the enormous spiritual harvest produced when Barovia finally breaks.

This makes Orcus temporarily useful. It also makes him catastrophic if he is allowed to “win.”

Why he notices the Unkindness

  • They have repeatedly died and returned.
  • They carried souls in coins and mechanical vessels.
  • They permanently killed Exethanter by finding the phylactery.
  • They restored Legna rather than surrendering him to death.
  • Thorgrinn remains a living contradiction: a soul in iron who continues to choose life.

Orcus calls them grave-thieves.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Orcus Interventions
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Initiative 20 / front beat

d6Intervention
1Bone Rain. DC 18 Dex; 4d8 piercing/necrotic, half on success.
2Denied Death. A corpse or destroyed undead rises as a 20-foot hazardous zone until next round.
3Soul Hook. Target a resurrected PC or soul-coin vessel; DC 18 Cha or Restrained by a 20-HP hook.
4Death Knell. Strahd cannot regenerate until initiative 20 next round. If the party knowingly benefits, +1 Orcus Attention.
5Infernal Challenge. Orcus and the pit fiend clash; if the fiend is deployed elsewhere, Orcus Pressure +1.
6The Horseman Looks Back. Orcus recognizes Thorgrinn and speaks the first line of the Black Road offer.
☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: When Orcus Is Beaten
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Do not make “0 HP” mean “you killed Orcus forever”

At 0 HP the manifestation kneels inside a storm of ash and gives the Unkindness a final choice.

Banish: destroy the manifestation violently. +2 Orcus Attention; future disposition = vengeful.

Permit withdrawal: refuse to feed the battlefield another death when the manifestation can no longer contest them. +1 Orcus Attention; disposition = indebted/curious.

Bargain: accept the Black Road, a death-mark, or a promise of later audience. +3 Orcus Attention; disposition = claimant.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 03D — VAMPYR: THE FIRST THIRST RETURNS
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/02 — Dark Powers

pages.name: What Vampyr Wants
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Vampyr is more personal

Vampyr does not arrive as a second demon army. It arrives inside the blood already spilled in Ravenloft.

It remembers Thorgrinn smashing the sarcophagus. It remembers the Unkindness refusing to inherit Strahd’s covenant. It regards Strahd as stolen property and the party as thieves who broke a sacred chain.

Its objective is therefore not merely to kill Strahd. It wants to reclaim, rebind, or replace him.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Vampyr Interventions
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Initiative 10 / front beat

d6Intervention
1Blood Tide. 20-foot zone becomes difficult terrain; DC 18 Con on entry or 3d8 necrotic.
2Black Sun. Non-artifact light vanishes. Artifact sunlight remains and points like a blade through the dark.
3Covenant Hook. Attach a tether to Strahd or a vampiric target. Three on Strahd threaten a rebind at 0 HP.
4Metal Dwarf. Thorgrinn is targeted by First Thirst despite having no ordinary blood; Vampyr drinks soul resonance instead.
5Possess the Wound. A destroyed bride’s mist becomes a Blood Heart unless artifact sunlight prevents it.
6Night Without Stars. Trigger Legna’s prophecy scene.
☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: When Vampyr Is Beaten
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The First Thirst cannot be solved by another sarcophagus in this scene

Banish: sever every visible blood tether and drive it screaming into the Mists. +2 Vampyr Attention; disposition = vengeful.

Allow withdrawal: stop attacking when the covenant has been broken and let the First Thirst leave empty-handed. +1 Vampyr Attention; disposition = obsessed.

Bargain: permit a mark, blood-debt, or future meeting in exchange for leaving Strahd unclaimed. +3 Vampyr Attention; disposition = possessive claimant.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00A — MADAM EVA: FIVE PROPHECIES COME DUE
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: Fulfilment Matrix
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Final Reading Was Not Decorative

PC / CardPromised testPayoff in the finale
Damien — HealerMercyA single heartbeat: preserve the life that prevents Vampyr/Orcus from stealing the ending, even when an exposed enemy could be struck instead.
Vesper — DivinerTruthSee who authored a “certain” future. Read the Unwritten; optionally let distant Vecna look back through the lantern.
Bunch — TraitorTrustReject “one must suffer so the others live.” Choose trust and let another person/ally make a free choice.
Legna — RavenDarknessDuring Night Without Stars, follow the silent black feather rather than the brightest supernatural violence.
Thorgrinn — HorsemanThe endingOrcus offers the Black Road that only Thorgrinn can walk. Choose ending, service, or the road back toward family.

Each fulfilled prophecy grants one Inspiration-equivalent reward and changes the battlefield once. Do not require the player to recite Madam Eva’s exact wording.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Damien — The Single Heartbeat
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

“Do not mistake the one who falls for the one who is lost.”

Run this after the pit fiend has meaningfully contained Orcus or during Strahd’s last phase.

Version A — the pit fiend: Orcus tears open the fiend’s infernal heart. It dies at the end of the next round. At the same time Orcus or Strahd is exposed. Damien can attack or preserve the ally.

Version B — the unforgivable patient: Vampyr begins consuming/rebinding Strahd at 0 HP. Strahd genuinely asks Damien to stop it. Damien can preserve Strahd for exactly one heartbeat so the Unkindness can kill him correctly. This is mercy without absolution.

Reward: if Damien chooses the saving hand for a reason larger than pity, cancel one Dark Power claim and grant the saved creature one immediate action.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Vesper — Who Wrote This?
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

“Ask instead… who has been permitted to write it.”

Once in the finale, describe three apparently inevitable outcomes. One is an authored lie or enforced fate.

Vesper may invoke Read the Unwritten. Tell her plainly which outcome is being imposed and by whom.

Then offer a second possibility as a whisper from impossibly far away: “Again?”

If she accepts the second vision, she gains another Read the Unwritten and Vecna Attention +2. This is not a trap hidden from the player; tell her something noticed her looking back.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Bunch — The Arithmetic of Monsters
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

“Only one of you must suffer so that the others might live.”

At a moment of real pressure, make a credible offer through a familiar voice—Finn, Strahd imitating Finn, or a Dark Power using a dead voice.

Examples: surrender one soul coin to seal Orcus; surrender the silver dragon egg to purchase Azrathox’s escape; let Vampyr claim Finn to release everyone else; allow one PC to inherit the covenant so Barovia survives.

If Bunch rejects the arithmetic and instead entrusts a meaningful choice to Finn, Azrathox, or another ally, that ally immediately changes fronts and acts. Mark the prophecy fulfilled.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Legna — The Smallest Sign
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

“Some allies do not arrive with trumpets.”

During Vampyr’s Night Without Stars, remove every visible point of reference except artifact sunlight and battlefield destruction.

Then describe one black feather travelling against the wind.

If Legna follows it, silent ravens gather on an invisible object: the true Blood Heart anchoring Vampyr. Expose it immediately; reduce Vampyr Claim by 2 and cancel the darkness when the Heart is destroyed.

The Raven Queen does not attack for him. She shows him the truth. He must act on it.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Thorgrinn — The Black Road
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

“A road that none of your companions can walk.”

Orcus recognizes Thorgrinn because death already took him and did not keep him.

“Metal is not life,” the horned shadow says. “And yet you insist.

You have crossed my road so many times that even the stones know your weight.

Come properly this time.”

During the final collapse a black road appears that only Thorgrinn can perceive clearly. Orcus may offer restoration to flesh, release from the soul coin, or service as a rider/champion. Do not make the promised restoration automatically trustworthy.

Accept: immediate Orcus route; +3 Orcus Attention.

Step onto it only to confront/refuse Orcus: +2 Orcus Attention and return if he succeeds at the scene’s challenge.

Refuse and remain with the Unkindness: the black road dies. During Barovia’s collapse, Baldrik’s recent Vistani route and the unopened keepsake box become the strongest surviving personal connection pulling Thorgrinn toward Ironfist territory.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00B — WHAT HUNTS THEM NEXT?
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: Dark Power Attention
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Attention is not approval

Track Vecna, Orcus, and Vampyr Attention. The highest result determines which released power has the strongest reason to pursue, tempt, recruit, or punish the Unkindness after Barovia.

ActionAttention
Directly defeat/banish a manifestation+2 to that power
Show mercy / permit withdrawal when you could continue+1 to that power; disposition becomes indebted, curious, or obsessed
Accept a bargain/mark/boon+3 to that power; disposition becomes claimant
Deliberately cooperate against Strahd or another power+1 to the assisted power
Use Vesper’s second forbidden vision+2 Vecna
Choose to pursue the escaped Vecna instead of either present power+3 Vecna
Thorgrinn accepts the Black Road+3 Orcus
Vampyr successfully marks a PC who voluntarily keeps the mark+2 Vampyr

Ties are good. A tie means a combined arc rather than a bookkeeping failure.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Campaign Routes
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Vecna Trail

The power that left first has been watching the others break loose. A high Vecna score means knowledge, authorship, the repeated timeline, and the question of who writes reality become the next cosmic problem.

Orcus Trail

Death notices the party that keeps returning. The pit fiend conflict, Legna’s resurrection, soul coins, and Thorgrinn’s body all become central. Orcus may hunt them from hatred or invite them because he cannot decide whether they are blasphemers or masterpieces.

Vampyr Trail

The covenant is broken but the First Thirst survives. Finn, Tatyana, Damien’s history with vampirism, and the possibility of new vampire lineages become the next problem.

Ironfist bridge

The Baldrik/Vistani route can still make Ironfist the immediate geographic arc. The highest Attention score becomes the cosmic shadow behind it or the campaign arc that follows, preserving the Thorgrinn homecoming without making the Dark Power choices irrelevant.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00C — THE UNKINDNESS: WHAT THE DARKNESS REMEMBERS
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: Major Achievements to Call Back
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Do not run the finale as if these are generic level-10 adventurers

  • They killed Mama Yaga after a near-total party loss.
  • They returned in soul-coin/mechanical bodies; Thorgrinn still remains mechanical.
  • They killed Baba Lysaga and her walking hut.
  • They restored Raven Queen shrines and released an ancient vampiric white dragon from corruption.
  • They learned the Order of the Silver Dragon’s failure and recovered the Tome of Strahd.
  • They learned that Strahd’s killer could become the next Strahd.
  • They defeated uncanny doubles and found graves bearing their own names.
  • They recovered a living silver dragon egg.
  • They recruited Azrathox instead of killing him.
  • They permanently destroyed Exethanter by finding the real phylactery.
  • They broke the Amber mechanisms and released/disabled the powers behind Strahd’s return.
  • They restored Legna through memory, soul coin, and the Raven Queen.
  • They know Barovia may die when Strahd finally dies—and chose to continue anyway.
☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Who Cares About What
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Strahd

He cares that they broke the loop and made his death real. His mockery should increasingly sound like someone trying to convince himself the old script still works.

Orcus

He cares about every denied death: the mechanical bodies, Legna, Exethanter, the vampiric dragon, and the fact the party repeatedly refuses to leave souls where death put them.

Vampyr

It cares that Damien became a vampire to save everyone and later escaped that state; that Finn remains contested; that Tatyana refuses ownership; and especially that Thorgrinn smashed its prison and refused the succession covenant.

Vecna

He cares about the Tome, the repeated loops, Vesper’s relationship to hidden truth, and whether the party realizes that prophecy and history are both forms of authored information.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: What Happened Immediately Before This Module Starts
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Nov 8 additions

  • Received Baldrik’s family-crested keepsake box from the Vistani.
  • Learned the group has repeated versions of this struggle across roughly forty subjective years inside the loop.
  • Received Madam Eva’s final five-card personal reading.
  • Prepared nine flasks of holy water.
  • Sent Tatyana a direct apology/message; she answered sounding frightened and more like Ireena.
  • Silvered Thorgrinn’s arm-mounted ammunition.
  • Met Saraphene and learned Strahd is afraid and Ravenloft divided.
  • Infiltrated Vallaki invisibly through guarded gates.
  • Finn escaped Wachter House injured.
  • Killed Lady Wachter and both sons after a failed attempt to capture/question them.
  • Recovered Luba’s Tarokka of Souls and Heward’s Handy Haversack.
  • Found shredded Strahd-marked papers in the basement.
  • Found Arl the pit fiend and accepted the substance of an infernal contract—without signing/releasing him yet.
☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 10A — DARK POWERS THROUGH THE STRAHD PHASES
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/03 — Strahd Boss Fight

pages.name: Phase I — The Count Uses Them
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Phase I modification

Strahd remains elegant and mocking, but the Dark Powers are now visible problems. At initiative 20 Orcus intervenes; at initiative 10 Vampyr intervenes unless contained by allies.

Strahd may spend one Legendary Action to attack a Dark Power anchor instead of a PC. If the party deliberately protects him so he can do it, that counts as a temporary alliance but not as mercy.

Key line: “You broke their cages. Surely you did not expect me to clean up after you.”

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: The Impossible Moment
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

When Dark Powers intersect the Strahd phases

Do not fire the Wish requirement too early. Let the bride gauntlet and early Strahd play establish the castle first.

Best timing: late Phase I through Phase III, when Orcus/Vampyr have been physically engaged or when one of them threatens to own Strahd’s death.

If a manifestation is reduced to 0 before the Wish, run Dark Power — Reconstitution. The impossible reform is the proof. Then make the djinn and/or Vecna routes available.

After the Edict of Finality, the same HP totals suddenly matter. This should feel like the party has finally made the battlefield obey mortal rules.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Phase II — The Castle Has Three Masters
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Phase II modification

The Heart Chains now matter to all sides.

  • Orcus wants the Blood Chain destroyed so Strahd can die.
  • Vampyr wants the Dominion Chain intact long enough to reattach its covenant.
  • Strahd wants whichever configuration kills the Unkindness first.

Let the party exploit those contradictions. Cleverly baiting Orcus into destroying a Heart Chain or Vampyr into preventing Strahd’s escape is exactly the sort of play this encounter is for.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Phase III — Nobody Gets Strahd for Free
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Phase III modification

Once Strahd is frightened of permanent death, both Dark Powers move to collect him.

Orcus: when Strahd first falls below 60 HP, Orcus attempts Death’s Due. If not stopped, Strahd loses regeneration and Orcus Pressure +1.

Vampyr: when Strahd first reaches 0 HP, if three Covenant Hooks are active it attempts to rebind him at 80 HP. The party has one round to sever a Hook or invoke Damien’s prophecy choice.

This makes “helping Strahd” for a heartbeat strategically possible without redeeming him. The Unkindness has spent the entire campaign learning that how he dies matters.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: After Strahd Falls
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Do not resolve the powers automatically

If Orcus and Vampyr are still present when Strahd dies, they turn on each other immediately over the released soul-energy of Barovia.

The party may flee, intervene, finish one manifestation, bargain, or show mercy. That final decision is what sets the Attention tracker.

If both are driven off, the collapse proceeds to the coffin/Barovia exit. If one remains dominant, it leaves a visible signature on the dissolving Mists and follows the party’s story beyond the Domain.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00D — THE WISH THAT MAKES VICTORY POSSIBLE
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: The Rule Above Hit Points
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

They are not boss monsters yet

Orcus and Vampyr have been released from the Amber Temple. Their bodies at Ravenloft are manifestations, but until reality is rewritten they remain connected to principles larger than a stat block.

Before Wish, the party can wound them, contain them, destroy anchors, force retreats and use them against Strahd. What they cannot do is produce a final victory by dealing enough damage.

The first time one reaches 0 HP, let everyone believe for a heartbeat that it worked.

The body comes apart. The castle shakes. For one impossible second there is silence.

Then the wound in reality opens again.

It is not healing.

It is being reasserted.

The manifestation reforms at roughly half HP. Increase its Pressure/Claim by 1. Then make the solution visible. Do not demand another full unwinnable grind.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: When the Wish Appears
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Dire need, not convenience

The two Wish routes should not appear at the start of the battle. Let the party earn the realization that ordinary victory is impossible.

Crisis triggerWhat it means
A Dark Power reaches 0 HP and reconstitutesThe party has proved that damage cannot finish it.
Orcus or Vampyr strikes the blow that drops StrahdA three-round claim window begins unless reality is rewritten.
At least two members of the Unkindness are down and an allied monster is failingThe battle genuinely looks lost.
Orcus Pressure and Vampyr Claim both reach 5+Both powers are close to dominating the ending.
The party discovers the rule through the Tome / Vesper’s prophecy before suffering itReward foresight: the offers can arrive before the first reconstitution.

At that moment Damien’s old djinn bond can flare. If Vecna has noticed the group—especially after Vesper’s prophecy or any earlier bargain—his voice may arrive at exactly the same time.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Route One — Damien’s Djinn
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Last Wish

Damien hears the voice before anyone sees the light.

“No. Absolutely not. I already paid that debt.”

A pause. Something enormous screams outside Ravenloft.

“Unfortunately, if that thing inherits this place, I suspect technicalities will cease to matter.”

Another pause.

“One. More. Wish. Then we are finished.”

The djinn has already granted its normal Wish. This is an emergency sacrifice of its remaining Wish-granting connection. The djinn wants to survive, not become a martyr.

If accepted: it grants one final Wish. The djinn survives, becomes unable to grant another Wish through this bond, and regards the extraordinary debt to Damien as settled. The djinn can flee once the domain begins collapsing.

If refused: do not punish the party. Vecna may still offer the second route, or the Unkindness may continue struggling until another crisis trigger.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Route Two — Vecna’s Borrowed Ending
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

A Wish from outside the page

Vecna does not return to Barovia. He is watching from another plane because the Unkindness has become interesting: they broke the loop that imprisoned Strahd, released powers that should have remained contained, permanently killed an ancient lich, and repeatedly violated the expected boundary between life and death.

A voice speaks from nowhere in the room.

Not loud. Not even close.

“You have discovered the difficulty.”

“This is not a creature you can kill.”

“It is a sentence reality continues to repeat.”

“I can give you another ending.”

Vecna can provide the Borrowed Ending: one effect equivalent to Wish. He requires a bargain. The price must be stated before acceptance.

Accepting the Wish bargain increases Vecna Attention by 1; actually using Vecna’s Wish increases it by a further 2.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: The Edict of Finality
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Recommended use of Wish

“I wish that, until Barovia passes from existence, no Dark Power released from the Amber Temple may anchor itself here, inherit Strahd’s prison, or return from destruction within this domain.”

Do not monkey-paw wording that clearly expresses this intent. The importance of the moment comes from changing reality, not tricking the players with grammar.

Mechanical effect

  • Orcus and Vampyr immediately lose Dark Power Reconstitution.
  • Destroyed Grave Horns and Blood Hearts can no longer reform.
  • Orcus/Vampyr cannot use Strahd’s death to become the new anchor of Barovia.
  • If either manifestation is already at 0 HP, it is immediately placed into its final ending state.
  • If it has reconstituted already, it keeps its current HP; the Wish does not refill or damage it.
  • At 0 HP, use the existing Banish / Spare / Bargain resolution.
  • The true multiversal Orcus or Vampyr is not erased. Their manifestation and claim here are what can now be defeated.

Every creature capable of understanding metaphysics immediately knows that something changed. Strahd should stop smiling.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: If a Dark Power Kills Strahd
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The three-round inheritance

If Orcus or Vampyr deals the blow that reduces Strahd to his final defeated state before the Edict exists, do not resolve the coffin chase normally.

Start a three-round Claim Clock.

  • Round 1: Strahd’s mist begins flowing toward the Dark Power instead of the coffin.
  • Round 2: Ravenloft responds to a possible new master. Orcus raises the dead architecture; Vampyr makes every wall pulse like a vein.
  • Round 3: without Wish or another truly equivalent metaphysical answer, the Dark Power inherits the anchor. Strahd is gone, but Barovia has not been freed. The Unkindness has won a battle and lost the ending.

Damien’s djinn recognizes this as an existential threat and may offer the Last Wish immediately. Vecna also understands exactly what is happening.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: If the Players Word It Differently
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Reward intent and cleverness

The players do not need to recite the recommended Edict.

Wish intentAdjudication
“Make Orcus and Vampyr mortal here.”Excellent. Both lose reconstitution until Barovia ends.
“No Dark Power can claim Strahd or Barovia.”Stops inheritance; also sever reconstitution if the wording clearly rejects their anchoring.
“Banish Orcus and Vampyr.”The Wish can eject both current manifestations immediately if they have already had their anchors meaningfully weakened; otherwise sever them and reduce each to a vulnerable final state rather than ending the entire finale for free.
“Kill Orcus.”It can destroy the manifestation, not erase the true demon prince from all planes. Vampyr remains unless included.
A highly creative equivalentPrefer the interpretation that preserves the enormity of the Wish and the players’ intent.

This is a campaign-defining 9th-level intervention. It should feel like reality obeyed—not like a technicality was discovered.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00E — VECNA: THE EYE BEYOND BAROVIA
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: Vecna Watches from Elsewhere
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

He does not come back to Barovia

Vecna has already escaped. Do not reduce that achievement by teleporting him back in as another combatant.

Instead, he watches the Unkindness from another plane. Their pattern is irresistible to him: impossible resurrections, soul coins, a permanently destroyed lich, the Tome’s revelation of repeated timelines, a broken Dark Power prison, and five people who keep doing the thing the story says they cannot do.

His presence should begin as an impossible observation: a sentence in the Tome that was not there before, an eye in a reflection, a whisper that only one PC hears, or Vesper looking too far beyond the final page.

Vecna does not initially want them dead. He wants to know what they will trade when certainty fails.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Personal Whispers
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Use only when the character is vulnerable

PCVecna’s line
Damien“You have already become a monster once to save them. Why become precious now?”
Vesper“You were told to ask who writes the future. You looked. I noticed.”
Bunch“Loyalty is simply a secret you have decided not to sell. Shall we test the price?”
Legna“Your Queen collects endings. I collect what endings conceal.”
Thorgrinn“A soul in a coin is still a secret in a box. I know something of boxes.”

These are invitations, not compulsions. A player must understand that accepting help also increases Vecna’s personal interest.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Emergency Deals
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Lesser bargains before the Wish

In dire need Vecna can offer a character one immediate intervention. Accepting any lesser deal increases Vecna Attention by 1.

OfferImmediate benefitConcrete price
Refuse DeathA character who would fall to 0 HP instead remains at 1 HP and ends one condition.Vecna takes one precious memory chosen by that player until Vecna is confronted.
The Unwritten StepTeleport up to 60 feet ignoring Ravenloft walls, wards and opportunity attacks.The character tells Vecna one true secret they have never knowingly given him.
Remembered PowerRecover one expended spell slot of the character’s highest available level, or one comparable once-per-rest class resource.Accept the Whispered Eye mark.
See the AuthorAutomatically identify the source of one illusion, false fate, possession or supernatural command and gain advantage on resisting it.Vecna is allowed to look through the character’s senses for one minute at a future moment chosen by the GM; never during private real-world player material.

Do not spam offers. One or two across the entire finale is enough to establish that he is watching.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Prices for the Borrowed Ending
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Wish bargain

For the full Borrowed Ending, state the price before the player accepts. Good prices create future campaign material without taking away the player’s current character.

Character-specific priceWhat Vecna gains
Damien gives the memory of why he first chose monstrosity to save the others.Vecna learns the emotional key to Damien’s self-sacrifice; the memory can become a future recovery quest.
Vesper accepts the Whispered Eye whenever she looks beyond written fate.Vecna gains a window into the campaign’s divinations.
Bunch gives Vecna one secret she has protected out of loyalty.Vecna learns something she valued more than victory.
Legna gives the first true name/title by which the Raven Queen recognized him.Vecna gains a dangerous fragment of Raven Queen lore—not control over her.
Thorgrinn allows Vecna to read the construction and inscriptions of his soul coin.Vecna learns how this particular soul-binding technology preserved identity.

If none fits the player, negotiate a similarly finite price. Avoid vague “you owe me anything later” bargains.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: What the Bargain Does to the Next Arc
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Interest becomes relationship

Merely being observed does not force a Vecna campaign. Accepted bargains do.

  • Refusing Vecna after hearing him: optionally +1 Attention if the refusal itself fascinates him.
  • Accepting a minor deal: +1 Vecna Attention.
  • Accepting the Borrowed Ending bargain: +1 Vecna Attention.
  • Casting the Wish through Vecna: +2 additional Vecna Attention.

Thus a Vecna-granted Wish usually adds +3 total, enough to make him a serious contender for the next cosmic arc without automatically overriding every Orcus/Vampyr choice.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 01 — VALLAKI: THE LOCKS ARE OPEN
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: 0 — From Wachter House to Van Richten
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The streets between them

The party is already inside Vallaki. Do not replay the gate infiltration. The route to Van Richten should take minutes, not hours.

You step out of Wachter House into a city that looks as though it has forgotten which revolution it is currently surviving.

Barricades divide streets that were open the last time you saw them. One junction is painted with wet red handprints. The next is hung with little bone spirals. Somewhere behind shuttered windows a child is crying. Somewhere else men are chanting the same six words over and over until they stop sounding like language.

No one seems to own Vallaki tonight.
☾ ◆ ☽

Show one Vampyr sign, one Orcus sign and one civilian consequence. Combat is optional unless the party chooses to intervene.

pages.name: 1 — A City Already at War
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Vallaki Before Ravenloft

The Unkindness reaches Van Richten only after seeing what the broken Amber seals are already doing to ordinary people. Lady Wachter and her sons are dead by the party's hand, but her death did not end the cult of Vampyr. It removed its command structure. Orcus' cult is exploiting the vacuum.

Vallaki no longer sounds like a frightened city. It sounds like two funerals trying to murder one another. Somewhere beyond the rooftops a bell tolls three times. A second bell answers from another district. Red cloth hangs from one barricade. White bone charms from the next. Between them, ordinary people have shuttered their doors and begun painting symbols over symbols, praying that whichever god notices first will mistake the house for someone else's.

What the streets show

  • Vampyr cultists smear thresholds with offered blood, call Lady Wachter a martyr, and promise that the First Thirst will choose a worthier vessel than Strahd.
  • Orcus cultists ring grave bells, decorate barricades with bone tokens, and proclaim that the only honest liberation from Barovia is death without return.
  • Civilians are trapped between them. The old political conflict has become theological possession.

This is not another Vallaki regime-change plot. It is the first symptom of a cosmological succession crisis.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 2 — Signs Across Barovia
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Dark Powers Are Being Answered

These are new finale symptoms Van Richten has gathered from refugees, hunters, ravens and Vistani travellers. Use two or three, not necessarily all of them.

  • Graves have opened without a necromancer nearby; some corpses simply stand and face west as though listening.
  • Animals have been found completely drained where no vampire spawn were seen.
  • The Mists have moved against Strahd's known will, closing roads he previously kept open.
  • People with no prior occult training dream the same symbols and wake knowing prayers they were never taught.
  • Ravens have abandoned certain roofs and crossroads entirely.
  • Old cult marks that had been decorative superstition now produce measurable magical residue.

The important change is not that people have become more fanatical. Something is answering them.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 3 — Van Richten: The Warning
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Van Richten’s Workshop — Final Briefing

He knows the party is coming only if they warned/contacted him. He has nevertheless barricaded the workshop because the city is in open factional violence.

Van Richten opens the door only far enough to see the first face. His eyes move immediately to the blood, the ash, the sealed letter and the infernal smell following you from Wachter House.

“Inside. Quickly.”

He locks three separate bolts behind you.

“Tell me you did not release another thing from the Amber Temple.”
☾ ◆ ☽

Let the players tell him. His reaction to Orcus and Vampyr is not “you fools”; it is the exhausted realization that the cost of making Strahd mortal has arrived early.

“You broke the locks. I am not telling you that was wrong. If Strahd was ever going to die properly, the prison had to be opened.

But locks do not distinguish between the prisoner you came to kill and the things imprisoned beside him.”
“Strahd von Zarovich may no longer be the most frightening thing living in Barovia.”

pages.name: 4 — What Van Richten Knows
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

What Van Richten can establish tonight

He knows

  • Wachter’s blood cult survives her death and is now leaderless.
  • A rival Orcus cult is openly active; grave charms and corpse rites are producing effects beyond normal cult magic.
  • Strahd’s control has weakened.
  • The Amber Temple’s old resurrection machinery has been damaged.

He can infer

  • Freed Dark Powers need anchors to act inside Barovia.
  • Strahd’s bond to the Domain makes his final death a potential inheritance event.
  • Killing him at the wrong moment could let Orcus or Vampyr claim the vacancy.
  • If a manifestation dies and simply returns, damage is attacking the symptom rather than the rule.

He cannot honestly promise

  • That Wish is definitely required. He can only tell them reality-altering magic may be necessary.
  • What Vecna is doing outside Barovia.
  • Which of the three tower clues Saraphene meant if the players ask about her dropped noun.
☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 5 — Do Not Let Them Own His Last Heartbeat
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Warning That Changes the Finale

Van Richten turns the map of Ravenloft toward you.

“If I am right, then killing Strahd is no longer enough.”

“Do not let one of those things kill him for you.”

“Do not let it take his body, his blood, his soul, his coffin, or whatever remains of the bond between him and this land.”

“You must control the ending.”

If the party asks how, he gives them a hunter's model:

  1. Find the Anchor. A god-sized thing cannot enter a small world without fastening itself to something.
  2. Break the Anchor. Destroying the manifestation without this is only buying time.
  3. Revoke the Claim. If the thing simply returns, then the problem is not hit points. The problem is what reality is allowing.
“And if you reach that point—if you kill something and the world simply puts it back—then you are beyond my profession.”

“You will need magic that does not wound reality.”

“You will need magic that tells reality it is wrong.”

He pauses.

“Wish, perhaps.”

“Gods help us, I hope I am being dramatic.”

This foreshadows the Edict of Finality without solving the encounter before the players actually witness Dark Power Reconstitution.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 6 — Optional: One Last Choice in Vallaki
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

They Cannot Save Every Street Before Ravenloft

After the warning, give the Unkindness a strategic choice. This is optional, but it makes the castle pressure tracks feel earned.

ChoiceImmediate ResultRavenloft Effect
Break a Vampyr blood riteFree captives and destroy a living blood-font.Vampyr Claim −1; Orcus Pressure +1 as its cult gains ground.
Destroy an Orcus grave reliquaryPrevent a district's dead from becoming an army.Orcus Pressure −1; Vampyr Claim +1 as blood-cult cells seize territory.
Evacuate civiliansNeither cult is strategically weakened, but dozens escape.No Pressure/Claim shift. Mark Mercy Before Victory; Damien may draw on it during his prophecy test.
Strike both ritualsA costly, high-risk intervention before Ravenloft.Orcus Pressure −1 and Vampyr Claim −1, but the GM should impose a real resource cost agreed from play (spell slots, consumables, injury or exhaustion).
Leave immediatelyPreserve strength for Ravenloft.No change. The war continues behind them.

Use the Vallaki — Prelude / Intervention macro to record this.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 7 — Departure for Ravenloft
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

What Van Richten gives them before they go

This is the payoff for the party’s stated plan to seek allies and diamonds.

  • Three 300 gp diamonds suitable for Revivify.
  • One 500 gp diamond for a more serious resurrection emergency if their magic supports it.
  • Two doses of anti-undead field reagent: advantage on one saving throw against a vampire or Dark Power effect.
  • A chalked diagram of Ravenloft’s known exterior approaches and a reminder that the front door being open is an invitation, not a weakness.
At the door, Van Richten stops you one last time.

“You have spent months learning how to kill Strahd.”

“Tonight, remember that the thing trying hardest to help you kill him may be the thing you most need to stop.”
If asked whether that means helping Strahd for a moment:

“A drowning wolf may share a rock with you. That does not make it a dog.”

He stays in Vallaki to keep the cult war from turning the whole city into an anchor while the Unkindness assaults Ravenloft.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00A — EXACT HANDOFF: WACHTER HOUSE
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: 1 — The Hidden Summoning Chamber
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Opening read-aloud

The painted circle still glows beneath Arl’s feet. Brimstone hangs in the air beneath a house whose owners are now dead upstairs. Somewhere above you, Vallaki is quiet in the wrong way—the silence between two mobs deciding where to march next.

Arl looks from Legna to Damien and then to the rest of the Unkindness.

“Recognition. Mutual protection. Freedom from this circle and the Wachters’ little leash. No future service.”

He bares far too many teeth.

“Write it properly.”
☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 2 — Finish the Contract
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Scene: Damien and Arl

Do not renegotiate from zero unless the players choose to. The previous session already accepted the substance.

Accepted terms

  1. Free Arl from the circle and Wachter control.
  2. Mutual non-harm between Arl and the Unkindness for the Ravenloft undertaking.
  3. Arl goes ahead to Ravenloft and materially assists in defeating its corrupt lord/forces.
  4. No future favour, soul or unspecified service from the Unkindness.
  5. Arl receives truthful recognition of his assistance in Strahd’s defeat.

Let Damien tighten wording. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation), Arcana, or appropriate noble/legal check may identify a dangerous ambiguity; success lets the player close it. Failure does not create a gotcha clause—the contract remains what the group actually negotiated.

Use Arl — Contract / Release.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 3 — Break the Circle
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Arl is released

The last line dries.

Arl places one claw against the inner edge of the summoning circle. For the first time, the paint burns from the inside out.

The house shudders. Every candle above you goes blue.

The pit fiend steps across the line, looks down at his own feet as though checking that reality still permits them to move, and exhales a column of smoke.

“Castle Ravenloft.”

He smiles.

“I shall go impose order.”
☾ ◆ ☽

Arl goes first because the party specifically wanted him to enter through the front and create a destructive distraction. He does not know Orcus will become his primary target yet.

pages.name: 4 — What They Leave the House With
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Continuity inventory

  • Strahd’s unopened sealed invitation.
  • Box of shredded papers bearing Strahd’s crest and black wax impression.
  • Luba’s Tarokka of Souls, found by Vesper.
  • Heward’s Handy Haversack, found by Thorgrinn; his Baldrik keepsake box can be stored inside.
  • The three Wachter corpses in Damien’s portable hole unless the party changes that.

No direct intact correspondence between Lady Wachter and Strahd was found in the house.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 5 — Next Destination: Van Richten
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Do not add another detour

The group already agreed where to go next: Van Richten’s workshop/house in Vallaki. They specifically wanted a safe place to read Strahd’s letter and discuss the Ravenloft plan.

Use the civil-war streets as atmosphere and a decision point. A random combat here risks spending the session on a problem the players have already chosen not to make their primary objective.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00B — ARL: THE CONTRACT BEFORE RAVENLOFT
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: 1 — Canonical Terms
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The deal already negotiated

Party consideration: release from the circle and Wachter control.

Arl consideration: mutual non-harm, direct/material assistance against Ravenloft and Strahd, and truthful written recognition of that aid.

Explicitly rejected: a future service owed by the group.

Not part of the deal: souls, infernal ownership of party members, secret punishment clauses or a retroactive favour.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 2 — Suggested Contract Text
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Player-facing draft

By mutual agreement between Arl and the five adventurers known as the Unkindness:

The Unkindness shall release Arl from the summoning circle beneath Wachter House and from such control as that household presently exercises over him.

From the moment of release until the present assault upon Castle Ravenloft is concluded, neither Arl nor any member of the Unkindness shall knowingly and intentionally inflict direct harm upon the other.

Arl shall proceed to Castle Ravenloft and materially assist in the defeat of Strahd von Zarovich and the hostile powers defending or corrupting his seat, according to Arl’s own methods so long as those methods do not violate the mutual protection above.

The Unkindness incurs no future service, soul-debt, open favour or unspecified obligation by this agreement.

If Arl materially assists in the defeat of Strahd von Zarovich, the surviving members of the Unkindness shall truthfully acknowledge that assistance in this contract and when directly asked by competent infernal authority.
☾ ◆ ☽

Let Damien edit this. Do not force this exact wording if the players produce better language.

pages.name: 3 — What Arl Does After Release
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Arrival at Ravenloft

Arl travels ahead and initially attacks Ravenloft’s defenders as contracted. When Orcus manifests, the pit fiend’s priorities change naturally: a demon-lord/Dark Power attempting to seize Barovia is a vastly more offensive cosmic problem.

Unless redirected, set Arl → Orcus when the War of Broken Gods begins.

If he survives, the recognition clause matters in the epilogue: the party can truthfully sign that Arl aided the defeat. This closes the contract without owing a future adventure hook unless you deliberately want one.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00C — STRAHD’S SEALED LETTER
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: 1 — It Is Still Sealed
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Current state

The party deliberately did not open this on the road. They joked that opening it might start a timer and decided to save it for Van Richten’s house. Treat that caution as real player choice.

Opening the letter does not secretly trigger an arbitrary countdown. The genuine countdown is Barovia’s destabilization after the Amber Temple.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 2 — Suggested Contents
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

When they finally open it

To the Unkindness,

You have broken my temple, murdered those I named family, stolen the dead from their endings, and convinced yourselves that this constitutes victory.

I will indulge the misunderstanding once more.

The gates of Ravenloft stand open. Enter as guests, and you may yet receive the courtesy you refused before. Enter as prey, and the castle shall entertain itself.

Finn has returned to me. Tatyana remains under my protection. My household is divided, my servants frightened, and the dead beneath my floors have begun whispering names that even I did not invite.

You wanted an ending.

Come before lesser things decide it for us.

— Strahd von Zarovich
☾ ◆ ☽

This text is new finale writing consistent with Saraphene’s delivery; the Nov 8 transcript establishes the invitation premise (“guests or prey”) but not the complete written contents.

pages.name: 3 — Van Richten’s Read
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

What the letter tells him

  • Strahd is frightened enough to admit instability indirectly.
  • He wants the Unkindness inside Ravenloft before Orcus/Vampyr can seize the initiative.
  • “Lesser things decide it for us” is arrogance, but it confirms that Strahd believes something else can now contest his ending.
  • Do not treat the open gates as safety. Treat them as Strahd trying to choose the battlefield.
☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00D — CONTINUITY LEDGER: WHAT THE PARTY ACTUALLY HAS
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: 1 — Party and Level
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

The Unkindness

Level 10: Damien, Vesper, Bunch, Legna and Thorgrinn.

Thorgrinn remains in his mechanical soul-coin body. Legna is restored to living flesh through the Raven Queen’s rite. Damien previously escaped vampirism. Do not homogenize their body states.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 2 — Major Relics / Tools
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Already possessed

  • Tome of Strahd.
  • Sun Sword / Sunblade.
  • Holy Symbol of Ravenkind.
  • Nine newly crafted flasks of holy water (3 Damien, 3 Vesper, 3 Legna).
  • Thorgrinn’s silver-shot arm modification.
  • Legna’s potion of fire giant strength from Thorgrinn.
  • Bunch’s Cloak of the Bat, Helm of Brilliance, Boots of Levitation and Stone of Controlling Earth Elementals as discussed at table.
  • Damien’s portable hole.
  • Two immovable rods were specifically raised as a possible castle-scaling plan.

Do not invent that any of these have been spent unless play spends them.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 3 — Allies and Their Current Locations
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Not all allies are physically together

  • Arl: still trapped at the exact campaign handoff; terms accepted, release pending.
  • Azrathox: ancient red dragon ally; deliberately stayed outside Vallaki and will rendezvous after the party exits.
  • Van Richten: next destination, not yet visited this session.
  • Raven Queen: patron/divine interest, not a combat NPC to deploy.
  • Vistani: cannot directly fight Strahd due their old pact; they intend to leave before the pocket collapses.
☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: 4 — People Still Unresolved
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Do not forget them

  • Finn: escaped Wachter House; visibly injured after the Amber Temple release.
  • Tatyana/Ireena: alive in Ravenloft, protected by Strahd, frightened, and intermittently more like her original self.
  • Saraphene: asked to survive and flee; may provide one final piece of court intelligence if useful.
  • The Abbot: survived earlier events and remains a possible Ravenloft complication, not automatically a combat boss.
  • Baldrik: left Barovia/Vistani business roughly a week earlier, toward Amphail and then the Sword Mountains; Thorgrinn has his unopened keepsake box.
☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 03X — BRIDE CONTINUITY: VOLENTA THE OATHBREAKER
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/03 — Brides & Castle Court

pages.name: Canon resolved
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Canon resolved: Volenta is the male Oathbreaker

The Nov 8 reading was intentional. There is no additional unnamed consort.

The established bride roster remains Ludmilla, Anastrasya and Volenta, but Volenta has been reinterpreted in Strahd1 as a male Oathbreaker paladin. He is the bride Madam Eva described as preferring seduction and a long drain over months rather than ravenous feeding.

  • Ludmilla: female, magic-user bride.
  • Anastrasya: female, ravenous/manipulative bride.
  • Volenta: male, Oathbreaker paladin bride; patient predation and martial pressure.

Do not create or deploy a fourth consort to reconcile the prophecy.

☾ ◆ ☽

journals.name: 00E — TWO-SESSION GM RUNBOOK
journals.folder: The Cat and the Unkindness/00 — Command Centre

pages.name: Session One — From the Cellar to Strahd
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Target: reach the physical Strahd appearance

BeatTarget timeStop if running long
Arl contract/release15 minNever cut; this is the exact cliffhanger
Van Richten route + letter20 minSkip street combat
Van Richten briefing/cache35 minUse field-note handout
Optional Vallaki intervention0–25 minResolve as challenge, not full battle
Azrathox + Dark Power arrival30–45 min3 rounds / one objective each front
Brides75–120 minUse retreat/surrender/mist rules
Abbot + Finn + Tatyana60–90 minEnd after “At last.”

The ideal cliffhanger is Strahd finally appearing in person after Finn/Tatyana resolve.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Session Two — Kill the Devil Correctly
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

Target: finish campaign

  1. Strahd’s courtesy/rest offer.
  2. Phase I: elegant Strahd.
  3. Phase II: castle/Heart Chains while Orcus/Vampyr interventions escalate.
  4. Demonstrate at least one Dark Power reconstitution if the party tries to finish it.
  5. Open Djinn/Vecna Wish routes only when defeat becomes real.
  6. Cast Wish → Edict of Finality.
  7. Phase III: frightened Strahd / Tatyana choice / prophecies.
  8. Coffin chase and final execution.
  9. Resolve Dark Power final dispositions and arc attention.
  10. Barovia collapse → keepsake box → Ironfist road.

Do not add another mandatory encounter after the coffin. The campaign should be allowed to end.

☾ ◆ ☽

pages.name: Failure That Still Creates a Campaign
pages.html:
☾ ◆ ☽

If the ending goes wrong

  • Orcus inherits: Strahd dies but Barovia becomes a kingdom of final death/necromantic dominion. End the campaign with the Unkindness escaping a newborn Orcus domain; Orcus becomes dominant next arc.
  • Vampyr inherits: Strahd is rebound/replaced and Barovia becomes a blood covenant under a new claimant. Vampyr dominates next arc.
  • Vecna saves them: Barovia can still be freed, but the price paid and +Vecna Attention make the next arc about authorship/secrets.
  • Party wipe: use the five prophecies, Raven Queen bond, djinn/Vecna offer or ally sacrifice only if it follows established choices. Do not simply reset the loop; they broke it.
☾ ◆ ☽
